sub_modules.title: Bacteria: Cell Envelope Architecture, Taxonomy & Quantitative Growth Kinetics
sub_modules.overview: Bacteria are metabolically versatile prokaryotes whose survival across diverse osmotic and chemical niches depends on a cross-linked peptidoglycan cell wall, specialized surface appendages, and tightly regulated exponential growth dynamics.

core_concepts.heading: Gram-Positive vs. Gram-Negative Cell Envelope & Peptidoglycan Biosynthesis
core_concepts.theory: Developed by Hans Christian Gram (1884), the Gram stain differentiates bacteria based on the physical thickness and outer-membrane permeability of their cell envelope. Both groups rely on Peptidoglycan (murein)—a rigid macromolecular sacculus composed of alternating N-acetylglucosamine (NAG) and N-acetylmuramic acid (NAM) linked by β-(1,4) glycosidic bonds (cleaved by lysozyme) and cross-linked via short stem peptides.
key_principles: Gram-Positive Envelope: Features a thick (20–80 nm) multi-layered peptidoglycan mesh threaded with negatively charged Teichoic Acids (covalently linked to NAM) and Lipoteichoic Acids (anchored to the plasma membrane), which bind divalent cations (Mg2+, Ca2+) and retain the Crystal Violet–Iodine complex during ethanol decolorization (staining purple). Cross-linking often uses a pentaglycine interbridge.

Gram-Negative Envelope: Features a thin (2–7 nm) single-layer peptidoglycan sheet housed within the Periplasmic Space, surrounded by an asymmetric Outer Membrane (OM). The inner leaflet of the OM consists of phospholipids, while the outer leaflet consists of Lipopolysaccharide (LPS = Lipid A endotoxin + Core polysaccharide + O-antigen). Trimeric Porin channels (OmpF/OmpC) allow passive diffusion of hydrophilic solutes <600 Da.

Peptidoglycan Transpeptidation & Antibiotic Targets: Cytoplasmic UDP-NAM-pentapeptide (terminating in D-Ala-D-Ala) is transferred to the Bactoprenol (C55 undecaprenyl pyrophosphate) lipid carrier to form Lipid II, flipped across the membrane, and polymerized by Penicillin-Binding Proteins (PBPs). β-Lactam antibiotics (penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems) are structural analogs of D-Ala-D-Ala that acylate the catalytic serine of PBPs, while Vancomycin binds the D-Ala-D-Ala substrate directly to sterically block transpeptidation.

core_concepts.heading: Bacterial Growth Phases, Monod Substrate Kinetics & Thermal Death Rules
core_concepts.theory: Bacteria divide asexualy by binary fission (mediated by the GTP-dependent FtsZ cytokinetic Z-ring). In a closed batch culture, growth progresses through four canonical phases, whereas an open continuous culture (chemostat) maintains indefinite exponential growth at a fixed dilution rate.
key_principles: Four Phases of Batch Culture: (1) Lag Phase: Metabolic adaptation, transcription of inducible enzymes (e.g., lac operon), and ATP/ribosome synthesis without net cell division; (2) Exponential (Log) Phase: Balanced growth at constant maximum specific growth rate (μ or k) and minimum generation time (g), where cells are most susceptible to β-lactam antibiotics; (3) Stationary Phase: Nutrient depletion and toxic waste accumulation cause growth rate to equal death rate (cryptic growth), triggering σ^S (RpoS) stress responses, secondary metabolite (antibiotic) synthesis, and endospore formation in Bacillus/Clostridium; (4) Death Phase: Exponential loss of viability.

Monod Growth Kinetics & Chemostat Steady State: Analogous to Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics, specific growth rate (μ) is a hyperbolic function of limiting substrate concentration [S]: μ = μ_max [S] / (K_s + [S]). In a chemostat, setting the dilution rate D = F/V (flow rate / culture volume) forces the steady-state growth rate μ to equal D (as long as D < D_crit).

Decimal Reduction Time (D-value) & Z-value in Sterilization: Thermal or chemical sterilization follows first-order logarithmic death kinetics. The D-value is the time (in minutes at a fixed temperature) required to reduce the viable microbial population by 90% (1-log10 reduction). The Z-value is the temperature increase (°C) required to reduce the D-value by 10-fold (1 log).

sub_modules.title: Virology: Capsid Geometry, Baltimore Classification & Replication Kinetics
sub_modules.overview: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites consisting of a DNA or RNA genome packaged inside a protein capsid (and optional lipid envelope) that hijack host translational and bioenergetic machinery to replicate via a one-step lytic or latent/lysogenic cycle.

core_concepts.heading: Virion Structural Symmetry & The Seven-Class Baltimore System
core_concepts.theory: Because viral genomes have limited coding capacity, capsids are constructed from repeating protein protomers arranged in either Helical Symmetry (rod/filamentous, e.g., Tobacco Mosaic Virus, Rabies, Ebola—where length is dictated by genome size) or Icosahedral Symmetry (20 equilateral triangular faces, 12 vertices with 5-fold rotational symmetry, and 30 edges, governed by Caspar-Klug Triangulation Number T = h² + hk + k²).
key_principles: David Baltimore's mRNA-Centric Classification (Classes I–VII): All viruses must synthesize positive-sense (+ssRNA) mRNA readable by host ribosomes. (I) dsDNA (Herpes, Adenovirus, T4 phage); (II) +ssDNA (Parvovirus, ΦX174 -> dsDNA intermediate); (III) dsRNA (Reovirus, Rotavirus -> virion-packaged RdRp); (IV) +ssRNA (Poliovirus, SARS-CoV-2, Dengue -> genome acts directly as mRNA); (V) -ssRNA (Influenza, Rabies, Measles, Ebola -> must carry virion RNA-dependent RNA polymerase [RdRp] to transcribe +mRNA first); (VI) +ssRNA Retrovirus (HIV-1 -> Reverse Transcriptase converts RNA to dsDNA provirus integrated by Integrase); (VII) Pararetrovirus / gapped dsDNA (Hepatitis B Virus -> replicates via an RNA pregenome intermediate using viral RT).

Infectious Naked Viral Genomes: Isolated, deproteinized genomic nucleic acid from Class IV (+ssRNA) viruses (e.g., Poliovirus) and most Class I nuclear dsDNA viruses is infectious when transfected into host cells because host ribosomes or host RNA Pol II can read them directly. Isolated Class V (-ssRNA) or Class III (dsRNA) naked RNA is NOT infectious without co-packaged viral RdRp.

core_concepts.heading: One-Step Viral Growth Curve, Burst Size & Temperate Phage Lysogeny
core_concepts.theory: Unlike bacteria (which double continuously by binary fission), viruses replicate by an assembly-line mechanism demonstrated in Ellis and Delbrück's (1939) One-Step Growth Experiment.
key_principles: Eclipse Period vs. Latent Period: Following viral adsorption and penetration, the Eclipse Period is the phase during which the capsid is uncoated and zero infectious virions can be detected even if the host cell is artificially lysed (chloroform treatment). Once new capsids and genomes self-assemble intracellularly (Maturation), the Eclipse Period ends. The Latent Period is the total time from infection until spontaneous host cell lysis releases extracellular virions into the medium.

Burst Size & Multiplicity of Infection (MOI): Burst Size is the average number of infectious virions (PFU) released per infected host cell (Total PFU at plateau / Number of infected cells). At a given MOI (ratio of virions to host cells), the fraction of cells receiving exactly k virions follows the Poisson distribution: P(k) = (m^k · e^-m) / k!.

Bacteriophage λ Lytic vs. Lysogenic Switch: Controlled by a bistable genetic toggle between the CI Repressor (maintains lysogeny as an integrated prophage by binding OR1/OR2) and Cro (drives lytic replication). Host DNA damage activates RecA coprotease, which stimulates CI autocleavage, flipping the switch to lytic induction.

sub_modules.title: Mycology: Fungal Cell Architecture, Dimorphism & Medical/Agricultural Importance
sub_modules.overview: Fungi are absorptive heterotrophic eukaryotes characterized by chitinous cell walls, ergosterol-containing plasma membranes, and both unicellular (yeast) and multicellular filamentous (hyphal/mycelial) growth forms.

core_concepts.heading: Fungal Ultrastructure, Dimorphic Switching & Selective Antifungal Targets
core_concepts.theory: Because fungi are eukaryotes (sharing 80S ribosomes, histone-packaged nuclear chromosomes, and mitochondria with human and plant hosts), selective chemotherapy targets biochemical pathways unique to the fungal cell envelope.
key_principles: Chitin & β-Glucan Cell Wall vs. Ergosterol Membrane: Fungal cell walls lack peptidoglycan and cellulose; instead, they consist of an inner load-bearing mesh of β-(1,4)-linked N-acetylglucosamine polymers (Chitin), a middle layer of branched β-(1,3)- and β-(1,6)-D-glucans, and an outer layer of mannoproteins. Fungal plasma membranes utilize Ergosterol rather than mammalian cholesterol.

Mechanisms of Antifungal Classes: (1) Polyenes (Amphotericin B, Nystatin) bind directly to membrane ergosterol to form transmembrane ion-leaking pores; (2) Azoles (Fluconazole, Voriconazole, agricultural Tebuconazole) inhibit Lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51), blocking ergosterol synthesis; (3) Allylamines (Terbinafine) inhibit Squalene epoxidase; (4) Echinocandins (Caspofungin, Micafungin) non-competitively inhibit β-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase (FKS1), causing osmotic lysis.

Thermal Dimorphism ('Mold in the Cold, Yeast in the Heat'): Systemic fungal pathogens (e.g., Histoplasma capsulatum, Blastomyces dermatitidis, Sporothrix schenckii) grow as saprophytic filamentous septate hyphae (mold) in soil at 25°C, but switch to parasitic budding yeasts at 37°C inside mammalian host tissues (Candida albicans forms invasive germ tubes and true hyphae at 37°C in serum).

sub_modules.title: Microbiomes: Human Holobiont, Soil Biogeochemistry & Plant Symbioses
sub_modules.overview: Microorganisms rarely exist as isolated monocultures in nature; they assemble into high-density, metabolically interdependent microbiomes that govern human mucosal immunity, global carbon/nitrogen biogeochemical cycles, and plant rhizosphere nutrition.

core_concepts.heading: The Human Microbiome, Short-Chain Fatty Acids & Colonization Resistance
core_concepts.theory: The human body harbors ~3.8 × 10^13 microbial cells (roughly a 1:1 ratio with human somatic cells, predominantly in the colon), encoding >100-fold more unique genes than the human genome.
key_principles: Dominant Gut Phyla & Fermentation Energetics: Dominated by strict anaerobes of the phyla Bacteroidota (Bacteroidetes) and Bacillota (Firmicutes), alongside Actinomycetota (Bifidobacterium) and Verrucomicrobiota (Akkermansia). Gut anaerobes ferment indigestible dietary plant polysaccharides into Short-Chain Fatty Acids (SCFAs: Acetate, Propionate, and Butyrate). Butyrate serves as the primary β-oxidation fuel for colonic epithelial cells (colonocytes) and inhibits histone deacetylases (HDACs) to induce Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs).

Colonization Resistance & Dysbiosis: Commensal microbiota exclude pathogens via bacteriocin secretion, nutrient competition, and secondary bile acid conversion (7α-dehydroxylation). Broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., clindamycin) collapse alpha-diversity, allowing endospore-forming Clostridioides difficile to germinate and secrete Toxins A and B (glucosyltransferases that inactivate host Rho GTPases).

core_concepts.heading: Plant-Microbe Symbioses: Rhizobium Nitrogen Fixation & Mycorrhizal Networks
core_concepts.theory: Plants recruit a specialized Rhizosphere Microbiome through root exudates (flavonoids, strigolactones, organic acids) to acquire growth-limiting mineral nutrients (N and P).
key_principles: Biological Nitrogen Fixation & The Oxygen Paradox: Atmospheric N2 (N≡N triple bond energy = 945 kJ/mol) is reduced to bioavailable ammonia (NH3) exclusively by prokaryotic Nitrogenase (dinitrogenase reductase Fe-protein + dinitrogenase MoFe-protein): N2 + 8 H+ + 8 e- + 16 MgATP -> 2 NH3 + H2 + 16 MgADP + 16 Pi. Because the Fe-S clusters of nitrogenase are irreversibly inactivated by O2, legume root nodules synthesize Leghemoglobin—an oxygen-buffering hemoprotein that maintains free O2 below 10 nM while delivering high O2 flux to bacteroid respiratory chains for ATP synthesis.

Nod Factor Signaling Cascade: Legume roots secrete specific Flavonoids that activate bacterial NodD transcription factors in Rhizobium/Bradyrhizobium. The bacteria synthesize lipochitooligosaccharide Nod Factors, which trigger root hair curling, infection thread invagination, and cortical cell dedifferentiation into a root nodule.

Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF - Glomeromycota): Stimulated by root Strigolactones, obligate biotrophic AMF penetrate root cortical cells to form finely branched Arbuscules (periarbuscular membrane interface), trading soil orthophosphate (Pi) and water for up to 20% of the plant's photosynthetically fixed carbon.

interactive_pins.label: Thick Peptidoglycan & PBPs
interactive_pins.detail: Up to 40 sheets of NAG-NAM cross-linked by Penicillin-Binding Proteins (transpeptidases). β-lactams mimic the D-Ala-D-Ala stem terminus.

interactive_pins.label: Outer Membrane LPS & Porins
interactive_pins.detail: Lipid A anchors LPS in the outer leaflet and triggers host macrophage TLR4 signaling. Trimeric β-barrel porins exclude large glycopeptides like Vancomycin (~1,450 Da).

interactive_pins.label: Exponential (Log) Phase Slope
interactive_pins.detail: Cell number doubles every generation time g: log10(N_t) = log10(N_0) + 0.301(t/g). Maximum sensitivity to cell-wall-active β-lactams.

interactive_pins.label: Viral Eclipse vs. Latent Period
interactive_pins.detail: During the Eclipse period, viral genomes are uncoated and replicating, so even artificial lysis yields 0 PFU. Intracellular virions appear at the end of Eclipse; extracellular virions appear at the end of the Latent period.

practice_problems.question: To determine the viable bacterial titer of a water sample, a microbiologist performs four sequential 1:100 dilutions (each transferring 0.1 mL into 9.9 mL of sterile saline) and spreads 0.1 mL (100 μL) from the 3rd dilution tube onto a nutrient agar plate. After incubation, 145 colonies are counted on the plate. What was the original bacterial concentration in CFU/mL?
practice_problems.collapsible_derivation: Each 1:100 dilution is a 10^-2 dilution factor. After three sequential 1:100 dilutions, the cumulative dilution factor in the 3rd tube is (10^-2)^3 = 10^-6. Plating 0.1 mL (10^-1 mL) introduces an additional 10-fold factor: CFU/mL = 145 / (0.1 mL × 10^-6) = 145 / 10^-7 = 1.45 × 10^9 CFU/mL.

practice_problems.question: What minimum Multiplicity of Infection (MOI = m) must a virologist use to ensure that at least 99.0% of the host cells in a culture dish are infected by at least one virus particle?
practice_problems.collapsible_derivation: If 99.0% of cells are infected [P(k ≥ 1) = 0.99], then the fraction of uninfected cells is P(0) = e^(-m) = 1 - 0.99 = 0.01. Taking the natural logarithm of both sides gives -m = ln(0.01) = -4.605, so m = 4.61 PFU/cell.

practice_problems.question: A patient with cryptococcal meningitis is treated with a combination of Amphotericin B and Flucytosine, followed by Fluconazole maintenance therapy. Why are both Amphotericin B and Fluconazole completely ineffective against bacterial infections (such as Streptococcus pneumoniae), except for Mycoplasma?
practice_problems.bold_answer: Amphotericin B binds Ergosterol and Fluconazole inhibits Lanosterol 14α-demethylase (ergosterol biosynthesis); bacteria lack sterols in their plasma membranes
practice_problems.collapsible_derivation: Fungal plasma membranes rely on ergosterol for structural integrity. Amphotericin B forms transmembrane pores by complexing with ergosterol, and Fluconazole blocks CYP51-mediated ergosterol synthesis. Because prokaryotic bacteria (with the exception of wall-less Mycoplasma that scavenge host cholesterol) lack membrane sterols entirely, both drugs have zero target in bacteria.

practice_problems.question: If purified, protein-free genomic RNA is extracted from Poliovirus (Baltimore Class IV, +ssRNA) and from Rabies virus (Baltimore Class V, -ssRNA) and separately electroporated into permissive mammalian host cells, which transfection will produce infectious progeny virions and why?
practice_problems.bold_answer: Only Poliovirus (+ssRNA) naked RNA is infectious; Rabies (-ssRNA) naked RNA is non-infectious
practice_problems.collapsible_derivation: Poliovirus has a positive-sense (+ssRNA) genome that serves directly as mRNA; host 80S ribosomes immediately translate it into the viral polyprotein (including the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase). Rabies virus has a negative-sense (-ssRNA) genome that cannot be translated by host ribosomes, and mammalian host cells lack any RNA-dependent RNA polymerase to transcribe -ssRNA into +mRNA; thus, Class V viruses require their virion-packaged RdRp protein to initiate infection.

case_study.title: Clinical & Agricultural Microbiology Case Study: MRSA MecA/PBP2a β-Lactam Resistance, C. difficile Dysbiosis & Rhizobium Inoculant Failure
case_study.scenario: Case A (Hospital Infectious Disease): A surgical patient treated with broad-spectrum cephalosporins develops a wound infection with Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) followed by severe pseudomembranous colitis caused by Clostridioides difficile. Case B (Agronomic Symbiosis): Soybeans planted in nitrogen-poor, high-nitrate fertilized soil fail to form pink, nitrogen-fixing root nodules despite inoculation with viable Bradyrhizobium japonicum.
case_study.mechanistic_analysis: In Case A, MRSA carries the mobile SCCmec cassette encoding mecA, which produces an alternative transpeptidase—Penicillin-Binding Protein 2a (PBP2a). PBP2a has a closed active-site cleft with ultra-low affinity for β-lactams, allowing peptidoglycan cross-linking to continue unhindered, while Vancomycin (which binds the D-Ala-D-Ala substrate peptide directly) remains effective. Simultaneously, cephalosporin therapy wipes out colonic Bacteroidota/Bacillota commensals, abolishing secondary bile acid conversion (deoxycholate/lithocholate normally inhibit C. difficile vegetative growth) while primary taurocholate triggers C. difficile endospore germination. In Case B, high soil nitrate (NO3-) activates plant autoregulation of nodulation (AON via CLE peptides and HAR1/SUNN receptor kinases), suppressing flavonoid exudation and blocking infection thread formation because symbiotic N2 fixation (16 ATP/N2) is bioenergetically more expensive than direct root nitrate assimilation.

quiz.question: Why does treatment of a Gram-negative septicemia patient with high-dose bactericidal cell-wall-lysing antibiotics sometimes trigger an acute worsening of fever, hypotension, and septic shock?
options: Gram-negative bacteria synthesize lipoteichoic acid superantigens when exposed to β-lactams

Massive lysis of the Gram-negative outer membrane releases Lipid A ( the hydrophobic anchor of Lipopolysaccharide, LPS), which binds host CD14/TLR4 receptors on macrophages to trigger a TNF-α / IL-1β / IL-6 cytokine storm
Antibiotic cleavage of porin channels depolarizes host vascular smooth muscle directly
Gram-negative peptidoglycan is converted into botulinum-like neurotoxins upon hydrolysis
quiz.explanation: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in the outer leaflet of the Gram-negative outer membrane contains Lipid A (endotoxin). Rapid bacteriolysis sheds large quantities of free LPS/Lipid A into the bloodstream, hyperactivating macrophage TLR4 signaling and inducing systemic vasodilation, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and septic shock.

quiz.question: During the Eclipse Period of a one-step bacteriophage lytic growth cycle, what is observed if the host cells are artificially lysed with chloroform and plated on a lawn of indicator bacteria?
options: The plaque count equals the final Burst Size because virions assemble immediately upon entry
Zero (or near-zero) infectious plaques are detected because the parental virions have uncoated their genomes into naked nucleic acid and progeny capsids have not yet assembled
The plaque count equals exactly the input Multiplicity of Infection (MOI)
The phage immediately converts into a lysogenic prophage
quiz.explanation: Upon penetration and uncoating, the parental virion disassembles to release its genome for replication and transcription. Until new structural capsid proteins package progeny genomes at the end of the Eclipse Period (Maturation), no intact infectious virions exist inside or outside the cell.

quiz.question: What is the primary physiological role of Leghemoglobin in the root nodules of nitrogen-fixing legumes?
options: It directly catalyzes the reduction of N2 to 2 NH3 in place of bacterial nitrogenase

It buffers free intracellular oxygen at nanomolar levels (<10 nM) to prevent O2 inactivation of the oxygen-labile Nitrogenase Fe-S clusters while facilitating high O2 flux to bacteroid respiratory chains for ATP synthesis
It transports fixed glutamine through the plant xylem to the leaves
It synthesizes lipochitooligosaccharide Nod factors on the root hair surface
quiz.explanation: Nitrogenase is rapidly and irreversibly destroyed by molecular O2, yet reducing N2 requires 16 MgATP per N2 generated by aerobic oxidative phosphorylation in the bacteroid. Leghemoglobin solves this 'Oxygen Paradox' by binding O2 tightly (keeping free [O2] < 10 nM) while delivering a high diffusive flux of O2 to high-affinity bacteroid cbb3 terminal oxidases.

research_corner.paper_title: The Growth of Bacteriophage (Ellis & Delbrück, 1939) & Structure and Function of the Human Gut Microbiome (The Human Microbiome Project Consortium, Nature 2012)

imrad_breakdown.abstract_summary: Ellis and Delbrück (1939) devised the One-Step Growth Experiment by diluting phage-infected bacteria after adsorption to prevent secondary reinfection, proving that viruses do not divide by binary fission but assemble intracellularly during a latent period before bursting. The HMP Consortium (2012) sequenced 16S rRNA and whole-metagenome shotgun reads across 242 healthy adults, revealing that while taxonomic species composition varies dramatically between individuals, core metabolic pathways (such as SCFA fermentation and vitamin biosynthesis) remain remarkably conserved.
imrad_breakdown.key_method: Synchronized phage adsorption, 1:10,000 dilution to halt re-adsorption, and timed plaque assays; 16S rRNA V3–V5 amplicon sequencing coupled with Illumina shotgun metagenomic functional profiling.
imrad_breakdown.critical_takeaway: Microbial kinetics (whether viral step-burst assembly or microbiome functional redundancy) obeys strict quantitative laws that govern host health, biotechnology fermentation, and ecosystem nutrient cycling.
